blocking_issues: COUNTRY-CONTEXT quality floor fails in both locales. After excluding fenced visual/code blocks and raw URLs, EN is approximately 1,565 substantive words and PT-BR approximately 1,104; each locale must contain at least 1,600 substantive words for dossiers dated on or after 2026-09-23.

EN/PT-BR semantic parity fails materially. PT-BR is substantially abridged relative to EN, omitting or weakening material qualifications and evidence, including the EN discussion of the Durand Line mechanism, the >75% grant-financing context, non-performing loans, women's medical-education transmission, explicit Pakistan/TTP versus Taliban competing claims, and several external-relations qualifications. The PT-BR pending deck also omits the EN deck's explicit women-and-girls restriction mechanism.

Current-data discipline is insufficient for a 29 September 2026 cutoff. The dossier foregrounds the December 2025 World Bank projection (2025 GDP +4.3%, population +8.6%, GDP per capita -4.0%) even though later World Bank 2026 material available before cutoff reports/estimates 2025 GDP growth at 4.8% and GDP per capita at -5.6%. A country dossier may discuss vintages, but must identify the older figures as superseded/projection-vintage data and reconcile them with the latest available official estimate rather than present the older projection as the current macro anchor.

The dossier's visual chart reproduces the superseded December-2025 projection without a vintage/revision comparison. Because the visual is a central macro visual, this can mislead readers about the latest available 2025 estimate at the stated cutoff.
required_fixes: Expand both locales above the 1,600-substantive-word floor with distinct, mechanism-bearing material rather than padding; preserve at least 12 analytical H2 sections and the existing visual floor.
Restore full semantic equivalence between EN and PT-BR, including material qualifications, attribution, transmission mechanisms, contrary evidence and metadata/deck meaning.

Re-run the macro factual pass using the latest World Bank 2026 releases available by the information cutoff. Distinguish December-2025 projections from later 2026 estimates/revisions; reconcile 4.3% versus 4.8% GDP growth and -4.0% versus -5.6% GDP-per-capita change, and update prose/visuals consistently in both locales.
Update the macro chart so its title/caption explicitly identifies data vintage/status, or replace it with the latest official estimate; do not mix vintages silently.
Re-check every current/time-sensitive claim after the macro update and preserve neutral attribution for contested security/political claims.
